decisions.reason: As a flagship product close to the core dosimetry business and visibly promoted since 2023, management is very unlikely to reverse a public commitment absent clear evidence of failure.

Because it builds on the established oncology QA offering and supports the announced direction toward integration, automation, and prediction, management is likely to continue backing it and treat any slow traction as temporary.

This CT image quality phantom fits the firm's medical imaging QA capabilities, so with the launch still recent management would usually keep it on the market to justify its development effort and give adoption more time.

Although this mammography phantom is more distant from the firm's core offer, it is still newly launched and the firm is expanding, so management is more likely to persist for now rather than quickly admit a mistaken move.

As another newly introduced mammography phantom outside the main strategic center, it faces the highest withdrawal risk, but escalation of commitment still makes near-term continuation more likely than an immediate exit.

This flagship imaging QA instrument line is publicly tied to the firm's stated direction and likely carries meaningful development and launch investment, so management will strongly prefer to retain it.
